goal: Implement an experimental, opt-in OpenAI fixed-greeting spoken interruption path using the existing reviewed provider-neutral LocalAudioPreRoll foundation. The user outcome is: while the fixed greeting is playing, accepted local speech stops the greeting first, then flushes exactly one bounded pre-roll before live microphone audio so the first user word is not intentionally dropped. Keep explicit Skip greeting as the reliable fallback. Add greetingInterruption?: false | true | BrowserVadOptions; omitted/false must preserve current runtime and bundle behavior, enabled config must validate synchronously, and runtime VAD/worklet setup failure must fall back to the existing non-interruptible microphone gate without failing voice or leaking greeting-period audio. Use a package-private greeting-interruption owner composed by GreetingPresentation; OpenAIAdapter should only prepare and attach the generated track and delegate lifecycle. Preserve at-most-once Engine/provider greeting history, immediate/transcript-confirmed post-greeting behavior, response arbitration, turn mode, privacy-safe diagnostics, exact cleanup, reconnect generation isolation, and raw-stream metering. Keep the option disabled in the demo. Add direct owner, adapter, race, fallback, teardown, docs fixture, default-off, real-device Not tested matrix, and acoustic-uncertainty tests/docs. Run package, demo, docs, and non-browser repository gates. Do not claim real-device self-echo rejection, VAD accuracy, first-phoneme retention, or latency from mocks.
